_comment: Canonical schema descriptor template (schema/<name>.json). A schema is a four-section Brique element (brique/objective/functional/subjective). The engine projects the descriptor as meaning but does not interpret or enforce the constraint language stored in functional. That section directly holds the gabarit of the constrained shape: either the four sections of a Brique element or arbitrary functional data. A gabarit field may be an admissible-value list, an empty list for an open value, a nested object, or a schema reference object containing schema_ref. Documentation keys prefixed with '_' are removed at instantiation; schema_ref and cardinality are semantic keys and must be preserved.

brique._comment: Required for reflexive projection (meaning queries, read.meaning). No field here is validated by the engine at runtime.

objective._comment: Optional. Projected by the reflexive meaning layer.
objective.name: <schema_name>
objective._name_note: Conventionally matches the schema filename without .json.
objective.description: One sentence describing what shape this schema constrains.

functional._comment: Constraint language opaque to the engine. Holds directly the gabarit of the shape constrained by this schema. For a Brique-element schema, reproduce the target element's brique/objective/functional/subjective sections here. For a data schema, describe the data shape directly here. Wrappers and tooling may interpret this gabarit for validation, composition, or generation.
functional._gabarit_note: Examples only; remove underscore-prefixed documentation keys when instantiating the schema. A list containing values expresses admissible values. An empty list means the field exists but its value remains open. A nested object describes a local nested shape. An object containing schema_ref reuses another canonical schema; schema_ref and cardinality are semantic keys and must never be stripped. A simple schema_ref resolves only in schema/ of the current context. An absolute Brique path such as /root/agentic/schema/message addresses a schema in another context. Resolution never searches parent contexts implicitly. cardinality accepts one or many and defaults to one. Optionality, nullability, conditional presence, expected type, intent, and constraints may remain documented with underscore-prefixed notes until dedicated semantic markers are introduced.

_subjective_note: Optional. Free-form space for subjective categorization. Add any key-value pairs meaningful to you or your team — tags, priority, notes, author opinions. The engine ignores this section entirely.
